plain: The Wilson memo is a leaked set of notes that describes a secret meeting between Admiral Thomas Wilson, then head of intelligence for the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and a physicist named Eric Davis. In it Wilson says he was shut out of a private company program studying UFO technology. The record dates it to 1997, though Michels and others place it in 2002. Michels says the two men met in the parking lot of EG&G, a defense contractor in Las Vegas, and that Wilson was furious at having no oversight of these rogue groups. He adds that the memo turned up among the papers of the astronaut Edgar Mitchell. Davis himself, one of the two men in the meeting, says the notes are '100% accurate.' He gives Wilson's words: Wilson met the program manager, security chief, lawyer and chief scientist, who after long arguing told him it was crash retrieval of 'non-human technology, off-world.' Others tell it from outside. The online researcher UAPGerb backs its core claim that Wilson was denied access, though he puts Wilson at the Defense Intelligence Agency, and he mentions a 'watch committee' of gatekeepers. The researcher Grant Cameron traces how the memo passed from Mitchell to a man named James Rigney in Australia and then to him, around 2019, and the filmmaker Jeremy Corbell says he knew about it early through Mitchell. If true, it would mean a private company held alien technology beyond the military's oversight.
